# posthog_platform_alert (Resource)

Manage an alert on PostHog's shared alerts platform. One resource covers every kind of alert, chosen by `source_kind`, and the settings that kind needs go in the block of the same name. `logs` is the only kind so far: it counts the log entries matching its filters over a rolling window and fires when that count crosses the threshold.

~> **One alert, one resource.** Do not manage an alert with this resource and with `posthog_logs_alert` at the same time. Both write the same alert, so each apply undoes the other's changes. The provider cannot detect this. To move an alert from `posthog_logs_alert`, use a `moved` block (see below) and remove the old resource in the same change.

The platform alerts API is behind the `platform-alerts` feature flag. Until it is on for your organization, every request fails with 403. The API key needs the Alert scope at write, plus the scope of each source kind it manages at write (Logs for `logs`). Write includes read. With the source kind's scope missing PostHog answers 404, and Terraform then plans to create the alert again.

Every optional setting has the default PostHog stores, declared here so it shows in the plan. Removing a setting from your configuration returns it to that default, and Terraform corrects an edit made in the PostHog UI.

An alert with no destination notifies nobody. A `logs` alert keeps a logs alert row beside it, whose id is `legacy_configuration_id`, so attach destinations with `posthog_logs_alert_destination` and `alert_id = posthog_platform_alert.<name>.legacy_configuration_id`.

**Moving from `posthog_logs_alert`.** With Terraform 1.8 and later, a `moved` block from the `posthog_logs_alert` address to this one adopts the alert with no destroy (see the example). The flat attributes move into the `logs` block: `severity_levels`, `service_names` and `filter_group_json` under `logs.filters`, `threshold_count`, `threshold_operator` and `window_minutes` under `logs.condition`. The rest keep their names. The alert must be one the platform already evaluates, which is true once its project has begun moving logs alerts to the platform. Otherwise the plan fails and names the alert. `snooze_until` is not managed by this resource, so a snooze stays as it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Fire when a service logs more than 10 errors in a 10-minute window, with one
# group per service so each service fires and resolves on its own.
resource "posthog_platform_alert" "checkout_errors" {
  name        = "Checkout API errors"
  source_kind = "logs"

  # Noise reduction: only fire once 2 of the last 3 checks have breached the
  # threshold, then wait 30 minutes before notifying again.
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  datapoints_to_alarm = 2
  cooldown_minutes    = 30

  # Quiet hours, in the project's timezone.
  blocked_windows = [{
    start = "22:00"
    end   = "06:00"
  }]

  grouping = {
    mode = "by_result_labels"
    keys = ["service_name"]
  }

  logs = {
    filters = {
      severity_levels = ["error", "fatal"]
      service_names   = ["checkout-api", "payments-api"]
    }
    condition = {
      threshold_count    = 10
      threshold_operator = "above"
      window_minutes     = 10
    }
  }
}

# A logs alert keeps a logs alert row beside it, so destinations attach through
# legacy_configuration_id.
resource "posthog_logs_alert_destination" "checkout_errors_oncall" {
  alert_id    = posthog_platform_alert.checkout_errors.legacy_configuration_id
  type        = "webhook"
  webhook_url = "https://example.com/hooks/oncall"
}

# Move an alert from posthog_logs_alert with no destroy (Terraform 1.8 and later).
# Remove the posthog_logs_alert block in the same change.
moved {
  from = posthog_logs_alert.server_errors
  to   = posthog_platform_alert.server_errors
}

resource "posthog_platform_alert" "server_errors" {
  name        = "5xx responses"
  source_kind = "logs"

  logs = {
    filters = {
      filter_group_json = jsonencode({
        type = "AND"
        values = [{
          type = "AND"
          values = [{
            type     = "log_attribute"
            key      = "status_code"
            operator = "exact"
            value    = ["500", "502", "503"]
          }]
        }]
      })
    }
    condition = {
      threshold_count = 50
      window_minutes  = 15
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `source_kind` (String) Product whose data the alert evaluates: `logs`. Changing it replaces the alert, because PostHog cannot change the kind of an existing alert. Set the block of the same name.

### Optional

- `blocked_windows` (Attributes Set) Quiet hours: time windows during which the alert does not notify. Times use the project timezone. Windows must not overlap or touch each other. A window may cross midnight (for example `22:00` to `06:00`), but only as the sole window, because PostHog stores a crossing window as two windows when anything else is configured. PostHog enforces its own limits on window length and count, and reports them on apply. Omit the attribute, or set it to an empty list, to disable quiet hours. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--blocked_windows))
- `cooldown_minutes` (Number) Minimum minutes between notifications for the same alert. Defaults to 0, meaning no cooldown.
- `datapoints_to_alarm` (Number) How many of the `evaluation_periods` most recent checks must breach before the alert fires. Must be between 1 and 10 and must not exceed `evaluation_periods`. Defaults to 1.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the alert is evaluated on schedule. Defaults to true. Disabling it ends any firing.
- `evaluation_periods` (Number) How many of the most recent checks to consider. A `logs` alert is checked every 5 minutes, so 3 periods cover the last 15 minutes. Must be between 1 and 10. Defaults to 1.
- `grouping` (Attributes) How the alert splits its results into groups that fire and resolve on their own. Defaults to one group for the whole alert.

~> **Changing `keys` drops every existing group silently.** PostHog deletes the groups and closes their notification threads without a message, so a group that was firing sends no resolve. The PostHog UI warns before this change. Terraform cannot, so check the plan. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grouping))
- `logs` (Attributes) Settings for a `logs` alert. Required when `source_kind = "logs"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logs))
- `name` (String) Human-readable name for the alert. Defaults to `Untitled alert`.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (environment) for this resource. Overrides the provider-level project_id.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the platform alert. Not the id of the `posthog_logs_alert` it may have moved from; that is `legacy_configuration_id`.
- `legacy_configuration_id` (String) Id of the source product's own alert behind this one. For `logs`, the id `posthog_logs_alert_destination` takes as `alert_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--blocked_windows"></a>
### Nested Schema for `blocked_windows`

Required:

- `end` (String) End time as `HH:MM` (24-hour, project timezone). Exclusive.
- `start` (String) Start time as `HH:MM` (24-hour, project timezone). Inclusive.


<a id="nestedatt--grouping"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grouping`

Optional:

- `keys` (List of String) Result labels whose values make a group. Empty for `single`, required for `by_result_labels`. A `logs` alert can group by `service_name` and `severity_text`, and only with `threshold_operator = "above"`.
- `max_instances` (Number) Most groups the alert keeps at once, from 1 to 100. Groups past it are not tracked. Defaults to 100.
- `mode` (String) `single` keeps one group for the whole alert. `by_result_labels` keeps one group per distinct value of the labels in `keys`. Defaults to `single`.
- `on_overflow` (String) What happens to groups past `max_instances`. `degrade_visible`, the only value, says in the last message how many were left out.


<a id="nestedatt--logs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logs`

Optional:

- `condition` (Attributes) The bound the count is checked against. Defaults to above 100 in 5 minutes, the defaults of `posthog_logs_alert`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logs--condition))
- `filters` (Attributes) The logs the alert counts. An enabled alert needs at least one of `severity_levels`, `service_names` or `filter_group_json`. Omit the attribute to save a disabled draft with no filters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logs--filters))

<a id="nestedatt--logs--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logs.condition`

Optional:

- `threshold_count` (Number) Log entry count to compare against. Defaults to 100. Use `0` with `above` to fire on any matching log.
- `threshold_operator` (String) Whether the alert fires when the count is `above` or `below` the threshold. Defaults to `above`.
- `window_minutes` (Number) Time window in minutes over which log entries are counted: `5`, `10`, `15`, `30`, or `60`. Defaults to 5.


<a id="nestedatt--logs--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logs.filters`

Optional:

- `filter_group_json` (String) Attribute-level filters as JSON, the same value `filter_group_json` takes on `posthog_logs_alert`. It stays JSON because a filter group nests property filters of many kinds. Must be a non-empty JSON object. Only the fields you declare are tracked, because PostHog annotates saved filters with defaults (such as `label`). A field you omit is therefore not tracked either.
- `service_names` (Set of String) Service names to scope the alert to.
- `severity_levels` (Set of String) Log severity levels to count: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, or `fatal`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import using: project_id/platform_alert_uuid
terraform import posthog_platform_alert.example 12345/your-platform-alert-uuid

# If project_id is configured at the provider level, you can omit it:
terraform import posthog_platform_alert.example your-platform-alert-uuid
```
